text:
How long does it take to get a passport once biometrics are done?
Fourteen (14) days as stipulated in the service charter.
heading: How long does it take to get a passport once biometrics are done?

text:
What happens if my date of birth or name differs between my ID and birth certificate?
Make the necessary correction by visiting either Civil Registration Services or the National Registration Bureau (NRB) before applying. The primary documents — birth certificate and national ID — must contain the same information.
heading: What happens if my date of birth or name differs between my ID and birth certificate?

text:
What happens if I discover I do not have all requirements on my appointment date?
You can reschedule the appointment to the next available date, or visit the customer care desk at your passport application centre for facilitation on submission and biometrics capture.
heading: What happens if I discover I do not have all requirements on my appointment date?

text:
Why must I bring physical documents when I already uploaded everything?
A passport is a security document; physical documents are required for multiple storage of record.
heading: Why must I bring physical documents when I already uploaded everything?

text:
Can someone else bring a child for biometrics?
Due to child protection laws, the biological parent must apply and present the child for biometrics, unless one has legal guardianship from the courts.
heading: Can someone else bring a child for biometrics?

text:
What is a consent form?
Authorization by the biological parent or legal guardian to the Directorate for a passport to be issued to a minor.
heading: What is a consent form?

text:
Can I renew or replace my passport outside the country?
Yes, through consular services at Kenya High Commissions and Embassies.
heading: Can I renew or replace my passport outside the country?

text:
How do I track the progress of my passport?
Log in to your eCitizen account, or SMS your application number (on your receipt) to 22222.
heading: How do I track the progress of my passport?

text:
Do I need a certified recommender's ID copy?
A recommender's ID copy is no longer a requirement.
heading: Do I need a certified recommender's ID copy?

text:
Can I collect my passport from a different centre than where I applied?
No. A passport is collected from the passport centre where you did your biometrics.
heading: Can I collect my passport from a different centre than where I applied?

text:
What do I need to collect my passport when it is ready?
Carry the invoice with a token attached and your original national ID. For a replacement, also bring the old passport booklet.
heading: What do I need to collect my passport when it is ready?

text:
Ordinary passport fees — how much a passport costs (best-supported figures, unverified)
The most consistent recent sources state the passport price as: A Series 34-page KES 7,550; B Series 50-page KES 9,550; C Series 66-page KES 12,050. Replacement of a lost or mutilated passport: KES 20,050. Payment via M-Pesa, Airtel Money, card, or online banking through the eCitizen gateway.
heading: Ordinary passport fees — how much a passport costs (best-supported figures, unverified)

Known conflicts between sources (demo material — do not resolve by guessing)
One source claims the 34-page and 50-page booklets were withdrawn in July 2026, leaving only the 66-page C Series at KES 12,500 — which conflicts with the KES 12,050 figure elsewhere and is uncorroborated. Another source still lists the 66-page passport at KES 4,550, the pre-March-2024 rate. A third lists an obsolete 32/48/64-page structure. The only authoritative answer is the fee shown on the live eCitizen payment step.

text:
Passport fees
The standard 34-page passport costs KES 7,550. Higher fees apply for larger booklets and special categories. The widely-remembered KES 4,550 figure is the pre-March-2024 rate and is outdated — budgeting for it leads to rejected applications. Payment is via M-Pesa, Airtel Money, card, or online banking through the eCitizen gateway. Two payment invoices are issued and both must be downloaded and printed.
heading: Passport fees
source: Njia knowledge pack (brief, to re-verify tonight)

text:
Processing timelines
Normal processing takes roughly 10 working days from biometric capture. Express processing (2-3 days) is available at Nyayo House.
heading: Processing timelines
source: Njia knowledge pack (brief, to re-verify tonight)

text:
Processing centres
Nine centres serve applicants: Nairobi (Nyayo House), Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Nakuru, Embu, Kisii, Kericho, and Bungoma. Diaspora applicants use the nearest Kenyan High Commission or Embassy. Applicants near Thika would typically book Nairobi (Nyayo House).
heading: Processing centres
source: Njia knowledge pack (brief, to re-verify tonight)

text:
Documents for a first-time adult applicant
Original birth certificate and copy. Original national ID and copy. Recent passport-size photograph with white background taken within the last six months. Printed eCitizen application form and both payment invoices. Name discrepancies between national ID and birth certificate cause significant problems and should be resolved before applying.
heading: Documents for a first-time adult applicant
source: Njia knowledge pack (brief, to re-verify tonight)

text:
Application flow
Register or log in on eCitizen at dis.ecitizen.go.ke, go to Directorate of Immigration Services, New Applications, complete Form 19 and upload documents, pay the fee, receive two payment invoices, book an appointment at a processing centre, attend in person for biometric capture, collect the passport once notified.
heading: Application flow
source: Njia knowledge pack (brief, to re-verify tonight)

text:
Kenya Passport and Travel Documents (official DIS page)
The Government of Kenya issues ePassports to citizens, valid for 10 years, in compliance with ICAO document 9303 and the East African Community Summit resolution.

Passport applicants apply online and pay requisite fees through the eCitizen portal at dis.ecitizen.go.ke. The various categories of Kenya passports and applicable fees are described on the DIS fees page.

Upon completing the application and paying applicable fees, applicants must book an appointment through the eCitizen portal and select one of the following Passport Processing Centres to submit applications and enrol biometrics (photo capture / biometric): Nairobi (Nyayo House), Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Nakuru, Embu, Kisii, Kericho and Bungoma.

Kenyan Diaspora in need of passport services may contact the nearest Kenya High Commission or Embassy for appointments and further assistance.
heading: Kenya Passport and Travel Documents (official DIS page)
